sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Indra Pratap Singh,Sandeep Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ashwini Kumar Tripathi
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Counter affidavit filed on behalf of the complainant/informant is taken on record.

2. Heard Shri Indra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the accused-applicant, Shri Ashwini Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the complainant/informant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Dayavati for grant of bail, in Case Crime/F.I.R. No. 0230 of 2022, under Sections 147, 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 323, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Khandasa, District Faizabad/Ayodhya, during trial.
4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.
Applicant is a lady and is purchaser of the property which is alleged to have been sold by the informant by registering a sale-deed for consideration of Rs. 20,000/-.

sentences.text:
It is vehemently submitted that even if the contents of the F.I.R. are believed as it is, it will emerge that informant is not aggrieved by the execution of the sale-deed rather he is aggrieved by the fact that Rs. 6,00,000/-, which according to the informant was residue consideration was required to be paid to him and instead of paying this consideration he was forced to believe that if he will invest this amount in a company he will receive double of the same within six years and on the lurement given by the accused persons, he became ready to deposit this amount in the company, however, the bond, which has been provided to him by the accused persons pertaining to the deposition of Rs.
6,00,000/- in that company has emerged as fake and fictitious.

6. It is further submitted that applicant is a lady and he is simply the purchaser of the land for consideration and this transaction has not been disputed by the informant and no specific role of any kind has been assigned to her with regard to the deposition of money of Rs. 6,00,000/- in the company, which has been attributed to the other accused persons.

7. It is vehemently submitted that co-accused persons, namely, Shiv Kumar Pandey as well as Ashish Kumar Pandey whose role in the alleged crime is graver than the role of the instant applicant, have been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated 25.07.2023 and 16.08.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 9342 of 2023 and 7778 of 2023, respectively.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 9342 of 2023 and 7778 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 8. It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 16.11.2023 and she is not having any criminal history.
The charged offences against the applicant are triable by Magistrate.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
9. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, she is not entitled to be released on bail.

10. Shri Ashwini Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the complainant/informant vehemently opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the informant has been deceived of Rs.
6,00,000/- in furtherance of a conspiracy hatched by all the accused persons and the instant applicant was also part and parcel of the said conspiracy.
11. Perusal of the record would reveal that it has not been denied by the informant that a sale-deed of the land was executed by him in favour of the applicant on 03.07.2019.

However, it is alleged that the said land was sold for Rs. 6,20,000/-, out of which, only Rs. 20,000/- were given to him and rest of the amount was promised to be given later on and the said amount on the pretext of investment in a company has been misappropriated by the accused persons.
The copy of the sale-deed available on record, would suggest that the land has been sold for Rs. 20,000/- without there being any other contemplation.
Applicant is a lady.
She is languishing in jail in this case since 16.11.2023 without any criminal antecedents.

Co-accused persons, namely, Shiv Kumar Pandey and Ashish Kumar Pandey whose role in the alleged crime is graver than the role of the instant applicant, have already been granted bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

13. Let the accused/applicant- Dayawati involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
